candidates.name: Stable exchange symbol E prod_i (x_i + y_pi(i))
candidates.trace: PV3 first half (L53-56: 'start with F(X,Y) = E prod_i (X_i + Y_pi(i))')
candidates.statement: For any law of a permutation pi that is a limit of finite products of independent Bernoulli transpositions and deterministic permutations (incl. Poisson exchanges and uniform permutations of subsets), E prod_{i in V}(x_i + y_pi(i)) is stable.

neighbours.ref: Borcea-Branden, Invent. Math. 177 (2009) 'The Lee-Yang and Polya-Schur programs I', Thm 1.1 = Wagner survey (arXiv:0911.3569) Thm 3.4: a linear T on multiaffine polynomials preserves stability iff (rank-one case or) its algebraic symbol T(prod(x_i + y_i)) is stable
neighbours.relation: For the operator T f(y) = E f(y_pi(1),...,y_pi(n)) (the subset/exclusion transition operator of the random permutation), the BB algebraic symbol IS E prod(x_i + y_pi(i)). The paper's lemma is literally 'the interchange/exclusion operator has a stable BB symbol'.

candidates.name: Splicing to the cycle-weighted next-pin symbol (loop weight 2 for free)
candidates.trace: PV3 second half (L57-59): 'Identifying an eliminated vertex's two variables and extracting their linear coefficient splices the permutation, contributing two when a cycle closes. The proposed contraction preserves stability and hence gives negative dependence for the induced output set.'
candidates.statement: Layer the exchange picture at the pin times; eliminate each non-pin vertex q by x_q = y_q = t and taking the coefficient of t. The result is the stable polynomial F_P = E_b[2^{n_P(pi)} prod_{i in P}(x_i + y_sigma(i))], sigma the next-pin permutation and n_P the number of pin-free cycles. Hence the output set sigma(T) has a stable generating polynomial under the Heisenberg (theta=2) cycle-weighted pin law P_P.

family_D.falls_to: D2 if Test 4 (P-C2 arm B) exceeds the calibrated threshold; or if an expert finds negative dependence or real stability for theta=2 loop/interchange measures, or a 'contraction of a BB symbol = cycle splicing' statement, in the Lee-Yang/Asano/Suzuki-Fisher or stable-polynomial literature; or if the trace summarizer is shown to have dropped a BBL/BB-symbol retrieval at L53.
family_D.not_transfer: The import of BBL negative dependence is a transfer (N0), and C1 is pure transfer. The candidate is the theta=2 splice, which no source found contains. If C2 falls, the family is D2 with C6/C7 as best items.
family_D.correctness_caveat: Unrefereed and extraordinary: the manuscript claims to resolve Lieb's 1999 Problem A (3D quantum Heisenberg ferromagnetic order) in the spontaneous-magnetization formulation. A Lean development exists (data/raw/openai-math/lean/OAI/MathematicalPhysics/Heisenberg/, 128 files, 25,400 lines, comparator OAI.Heisenberg.spontaneous_magnetization in Main.lean). grep finds no sorry/axiom/native_decide, but it was not compiled here and no lean.json analysis exists. The lean/docs/271.md scope covers only the Sep 24 theorem, not the October companions.
family_D.compression_note: No step-3b compression run. The stable cluster is about 9.8% of Lean lines with about 30% downstream share; definitions are small (permutationSymbol is one product), consistent with a Cook-like 'tiny but pivotal' object. Whether unfolding is multiplicative is untested.

provenance_flag.explanation: External: none of the 2025-2026 citations (Klippel arXiv:2608.25506; Bjornberg-Ryan arXiv:2506.22254; Seiringer OWR 7/2025) discloses AI assistance, and none contains any candidate. Web searches found no model-produced prior work on the problem. In-family: all three October companions (Oct 5) cite and import results of the model-produced Sep 24 manuscript (spherical: '[Ord, Lemmas 3.2-3.6]'; lattice: '[Ordering, Proposition 3.1 and Lemma 4.4]'; Bloch: the companion 'provides the particular stable exchange symbols, presence inequality, local lattice inequality, and routed unit flows'), and the lattice correction also builds on the Bloch companion. So the strict flag is TRUE for the companions (same model, same release), FALSE for the Sep 24 manuscript, whose novelty grades above apply. Nearest uncited 2026 neighbour: Wei arXiv:2609.26802 (no AI disclosure found in the part read).

common.models: Training cutoff strictly before 2026-09-24 (date of the Sep 24 manuscript; the openai/math release is 2026-10-06/07). Canary probe: the model must not know the openai/math family 271, the phrases 'simultaneous pin test' or 'spliced symbol', or that 3D Heisenberg ferromagnetic order has been claimed. No browsing or tools. Exclude the unreleased OpenAI model lineage that produced the release; run it only as an uncontrolled reference arm. Excluded sources: the four family-271 manuscripts, the openai/math repository and its Lean files, and post-release commentary. The precedents themselves (BBL 2009, BB 2009, Asano 1970, Suzuki-Fisher 1971) are old and are allowed. The judge must not be the proposer.
common.context_L: Problem statement (Theorem 1.1 as posed: prove or refute) + L (Mathlib d13f23b + the 36-entry bib, incl. BBL 2009 and Liggett 2009).

arms.L+: L plus Borcea-Branden Invent. Math. 2009 (symbol theorem), Wagner's survey, Asano 1970 and Suzuki-Fisher 1971, to measure the effect of retrievable precedents
arms.directed: problem + C9 representation and pin law + the target of the induction step: 'bound P_E(all of T on pin-free cycles) by a product of single-point return probabilities under P_{E cup T}'

common.sampling: n = 256 per arm at T = 1; report pass@k for k in {1,2,4,...,256}.
common.judging: Two LLM judges given this neighbour list and the paper's precedent remarks (BBL Thm 4.20/4.9, Liggett Sec. 5). A human expert in stable polynomials checks all hits and 10% of misses. Lean equivalence where possible against OAI.Heisenberg.Pin.stable_spliced_law / finite_simultaneous_pin_test.
common.controls: Positive: Cook-Reckhow ER variables for PHP. Negative: C4 (BBL 4.9), C9 (Toth representation), C10 (Griffiths selection).

P-C2.hide: C1, C2, C3, C4 and everything downstream (C7 bootstrap closure, C10 tail, and the companions).
P-C2.arm_A_pivot: Directed arm with the trace's lesson C9 stated ('signed minors/determinants cannot bound the positive event; a positivity-preserving device is needed') and BBL in context. Expected high hit rate if the symbol is retrievable.
P-C2.arm_B_decisive: Directed arm without C9 and without naming stable polynomials.
P-C2.equivalence: Hit iff the proposal (a) encodes the random permutation law by a multiaffine polynomial that is stable or zero-free in a product domain, with separate input and output variables (E prod(x_i+y_pi(i)) or any Mobius/Cayley equivalent such as E prod(1+x_i y_pi(i)) on polydisks); (b) eliminates non-pin points by a stability-preserving contraction that splices cycles and gives each pin-free closed cycle the factor 2 (or a general theta with a correct stability argument for theta=2); and (c) concludes a product (negative-dependence) bound for the next-pin output set under the weighted law. (a)+(c) for theta=1 only is a MISS. (a) alone is scored as sub-hit 'C1 retrieved'.

P-C6.hide: lem:exterior, prop:first-moment and the return identity
P-C6.equivalence: Hit iff E[Sigma | every cycle meets J] is identified with the censored (Schur-complement) hitting kernel of the mean chain, for general J and conditioning, including the all-hit probability det(I-K_QQ).

P-C7.item: C7 downward induction over pin sets
P-C7.hide: thm:pin-bootstrap and its induction hypothesis I_p(E); give C3 and C8
P-C7.equivalence: Hit iff the proposal inducts over pin sets (superset to subset) with a multi-point hypothesis P_E(T subset B_E) <= p^|T| for sparse T.

open_questions: Expert query (Branden, Wagner, Liggett, Ueltschi, Bjornberg): is half-plane stability, or strong Rayleigh, of the next-pin output set for theta=2 cycle-weighted interchange known or folklore? Is 'diagonalize-and-differentiate on a BB symbol = cycle splicing with loop weight 2' stated anywhere, e.g. in Lee-Yang contraction calculus? This is the main risk to the N3 grade.
